name: Nulldrift
description: Nulldrift is a targeted proprioceptive and interoceptive suppressor that severs conscious awareness from bodily sensation, including cyberware and chrome feedback. Users experience themselves as pure consciousness floating free of physical form — chrome, pain, hunger, and physical limitation simply cease to register. It is the drug of choice for heavily augmented individuals who experience body dysmorphia or sensory overload from their implants.
effects: Complete disconnection from physical body sensation
Suppression of all chrome and cyberware feedback signals
Profound sense of weightlessness and formlessness
Freedom from chronic pain associated with augmentation
Calm, directionless euphoria described as 'existing without needing to be anywhere'
side_effects: Complete inability to operate cyberware during dose
Physical vulnerability — users cannot respond to injury or danger they cannot feel
Disorientation upon re-entry to body sensation
Psychological: some users develop a genuine aversion to their physical body post-experience, worsening body dysmorphia long-term
cultural_context: Nulldrift is the drug of the augmented poor — Shelf residents who have basic chrome installed for labor but experience it as a burden rather than an enhancement. In communities where cheap cyberware causes constant low-grade pain, phantom limb phenomena, or sensory interference, Nulldrift is as much medication as recreation. Nightshade sells it legally as an industrial anxiety compound with a thin legal fiction; everyone knows what it's actually for. Among Tier 3 chrome-enthusiasts, a cleaner version called 'the Shed' circulates as a luxury reset experience.
story_hooks: A Shelf labor collective has begun collectively Nulldrifting on shift breaks — and a corporate enforcer has been sent to suppress what management calls a 'productivity crisis,' but which a labor organizer calls a 'dignity crisis'

A Nulldrift user who was floating during a raid woke up to find she had been moved, her chrome removed, and no memory of the intervening hours — someone needed her body to go somewhere while she wasn't using it

Nightshade's Nulldrift formula has been modified in a recent batch — it no longer just suppresses chrome feedback, it actively interfaces with it, and users are waking up with their cyberware reconfigured in ways they didn't authorize
